newsitem.title: GREECE: BANK/GREECE OFFERS O/N HELP, SHORTS STILL FIRM.
newsitem.headline: BANK/GREECE OFFERS O/N HELP, SHORTS STILL FIRM.

text.p: ATHENS, Sept 30 (September) - The Bank of Greece offered a round of assistance in overnight money to local banks at 13.40 percent but it was insufficient to relieve the liquidity squeeze and very short rates still traded between 14 and 15 percent, bankers said.

"The central bank offered overnight funds at 13.40 percent for the full amount of each commercial bank's overnight facility and additional funds for 80 percent of the amount of state securities issued on September 30 and deposited as a collateral," said a dealer at a bank.

"The conditions with regard to the specific debt paper are somewhat stringent and as a result they have taken some, but not all, pressure off," he said. "Overnight and tomnext rates continue to trade between 14 and 15 percent."
The intervention of the central bank provided greater help to local private and state banks than to foreign banks which have smaller facilities with the Bank of Greece, dealers said.
"It would help if the central bank held a competitive seven-day repo tomorrow," said a dealer at a private bank.
Three-, six- and 12-month T-bills go on sale today at unchanged rates of 11.90 percent, 12.10 percent and 12.70 percent respectively.

Liquidity is said to be squeezed further by the fiannce ministry's FRN private placement of 830 billion drachmas with five local banks and a T-bill private placememnt of 300 billion drachmas with a large state bank, dealers said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
